note: REP may be a function, and kg's `replace-regexp-in-string' held five temporaries across the `funcall' of it.  `limit' is the one whose capture raised outright -- (wrong-type-argument number-or-marker-p "b") -- because the loop compares it.  Emacs' own definition is Lisp too, in subr.el, and is immune for a reason kg does not have: it is byte-compiled under lexical-binding, so its locals became stack slots before any user `defvar' could mark the name.
